# Write a handler, an adapter or an extension file

<!-- description: Every name a step handler, a service adapter, a processor or an extension file uses from @sensigo/realm, each with its declaration. -->

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-library-reference.mjs from the API reports and the built declarations; do not edit by hand: after `npm run build`, run `npm run docs:library`. -->

A step's own work runs in a step handler (`StepHandler`), a call to an outside service in a service adapter (`ServiceAdapter`), and a project's extension file exports them for `realm.yaml` to name. This page lists the interfaces such code implements, the helper functions it can call, the error it throws (`WorkflowError`), and every type their declarations refer to that no other page holds first.

Where the docs teach it: [Handlers](../handlers.md), [Project extensions](../project-extensions.md).

| Name | Kind | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`compareStrings`](#comparestrings) | function | Compares two strings using a specified match mode. |
| [`countResults`](#countresults) | function | Counts accepted and rejected candidates and adds a candidates_found total. |
| [`createDefaultRegistry`](#createdefaultregistry) | function | Returns an ExtensionRegistry pre-populated with Realm's config-less built-ins: the adapter `FileSystemAdapter` under `'filesystem'` and the handler `CheckQuotesHandler` under `'check_quotes'`. |
| [`declareReleaseLine`](#declarereleaseline) | function | Declares that a host's store class (or plain-object store) belongs to this copy of realm. |
| [`locateQuote`](#locatequote) | function | Locates `quote` in `source` (the ladder above). |
| [`partitionBySubstring`](#partitionbysubstring) | function | Partitions a list of candidate objects into accepted and rejected groups. |
| [`resolveResource`](#resolveresource) | function | Reads a named field from a prior step's output stored in context.resources. |
| [`walkField`](#walkfield) | function | Recursively walks any value and collects all objects that contain a property named fieldName. |
| [`WorkflowError`](#workflowerror) | class | The error Realm throws and records, carrying a code, a category and what the agent does next. |
| [`AnswererMismatchFacts`](#answerermismatchfacts) | interface | The facts of an answer refused because its sender may not answer the question: the names that may, and the account the channel reported. |
| [`Base`](#base) | interface | What every way carries: its verb and the conditions it is offered with; each way type adds its own fields to it. |
| [`DueExpiry`](#dueexpiry) | interface | An open question whose time is up and whose `on_expiry` the engine can carry out (`expiry_due`). |
| [`ErrorFactsByCode`](#errorfactsbycode) | interface | The error codes whose facts are typed: one facts type per code, entering with the unit that types it. |
| [`ExtensionIdentityEntry`](#extensionidentityentry) | interface | One point-in-time identity of the extension code executing a run. |
| [`ExtensionIdentityModule`](#extensionidentitymodule) | interface | One loaded extension module's identity. |
| [`ExtensionIdentitySignals`](#extensionidentitysignals) | interface | Labeled advisory signals — each independently fail-soft; never part of the comparison. |
| [`ExtensionIdentityTree`](#extensionidentitytree) | interface | Versioned deterministic directory-tree fingerprint over the module roots. |
| [`FactsByCode`](#factsbycode) | interface | The typed facts of each unavailable code (`FactsOf`). |
| [`LoaderWarning`](#loaderwarning) | interface | A single structured diagnostic. |
| [`NewerDefinitionFacts`](#newerdefinitionfacts) | interface | The facts of a registered workflow copy written by a later Realm: the copy's path, the definition format it states, and the latest this version reads. |
| [`PreconditionFacts`](#preconditionfacts) | interface | A failed precondition: its expression and the value read, escaped and bounded (`PreClaimRefused.precondition`). |
| [`Processor`](#processor) | interface | A program's step that changes content, registered under its `id` and run in order by `runPipeline`. |
| [`ProcessorInput`](#processorinput) | interface | The text and metadata a processor is given (`Processor.process`). |
| [`ProcessorOutput`](#processoroutput) | interface | The text and metadata a processor returns; the next processor in the pipeline is given it. |
| [`QuoteCheck`](#quotecheck) | interface | What `locateQuote` returns for a quote: how it was found, where each part is, how often it occurs, and the nearest piece when it was not found. |
| [`QuoteSpan`](#quotespan) | interface | A span of the original source: `source.slice(start, end)`. |

| [`RateLimiter`](#ratelimiter) | interface | Controls the rate at which requests are sent to an external service. |

| [`ServiceResponse`](#serviceresponse) | interface | What a service adapter's call returns: the HTTP status and the data (`ServiceAdapter`'s methods). |
| [`StableBoundary`](#stableboundary) | interface | Where a rendered text stops repeating between runs, in UTF-16 code units. |
| [`StepBrief`](#stepbrief) | interface | What a `run_step` way says about its step: its kind, its description, the prompt the agent reads, the input schema an agent's answer must fit, and its handler. |
| [`StepContext`](#stepcontext) | interface | What a handler is told about the run: its id and params, the step's `config`, and earlier steps' outputs in `resources`, keyed by step id (`StepHandler.execute`'s second argument). |

| [`StepHandlerInputs`](#stephandlerinputs) | interface | What a handler is given as input: the step's params, after its `input_map` when it has one (`StepHandler.execute`'s first argument). |
| [`StepHandlerResult`](#stephandlerresult) | interface | What a handler returns: the step's output, and optionally a state update, a clean abort or a warning (`StepHandler.execute`'s result). |
| [`UnreadableRunFilesFacts`](#unreadablerunfilesfacts) | interface | What `unreadableRunFilesError` carries: the command that did not run, the runs folder, and every run file it could not read. |
| [`ValidationErrorFacts`](#validationerrorfacts) | interface | The typed facts of a refused answer: the validator's rows, their total before the cap, and, for an agent step's counted rejection, the countdown. |
| [`WorkflowErrorOptions`](#workflowerroroptions) | interface | What a `WorkflowError` is built with: its code and category, what the agent does next, whether it may be tried again, and the optional facts, step and ways on. |
| [`AbandonWay`](#abandonway) | type | End the run. |
| [`AdvanceWay`](#advanceway) | type | Have the engine carry out what it owes: a due expiry first, then steps. |
| [`AgentAction`](#agentaction) | type | What an agent does next, decided by the engine (`WorkflowError.agentAction`). |
| [`Cond`](#cond) | type | A condition a way is offered with: a way offered with a condition is admitted only when the condition is met (`Base.conditions`). |
| [`CondTag`](#condtag) | type | Who discharges a condition outside Realm; `client` is the MCP client's own approval prompt (`Cond`'s `client_prompt` member). |
| [`DefinitionAbsence`](#definitionabsence) | type | Why a run's workflow definition could not be had: never registered, an agent's copy gone, unreadable, not a valid workflow, an older or a later format, or not read. |
| [`ErrorCategory`](#errorcategory) | type | The broad kind of failure a `WorkflowError` reports: network, an outside service, the run's state, invalid input, the engine itself, or a resource (`WorkflowError.category`). |
| [`ErrorFacts`](#errorfacts) | type | Any typed error facts. |
| [`FactsOf`](#factsof) | type | The typed facts an `Unavailable` entry carries for its code (`Unavailable.facts`). |
| [`InspectWay`](#inspectway) | type | Read the run's record. |
| [`LeaseFact`](#leasefact) | type | What a probe found. |
| [`LeaseProbeReason`](#leaseprobereason) | type | Why a probe could not say whether a claim lease is held (`LeaseFact`'s `unknown` state). |
| [`LoadErrorCode`](#loaderrorcode) | type | The code a failed load of a program's project code carries: the error's catalogue code, or `uncoded`. |
| [`NoRemedy`](#noremedy) | type | Why an `Unavailable` entry offers no way on, with the cause's own facts (`Unavailable.no_remedy`). |
| [`PresentWay`](#presentway) | type | Show the open question again, as a form in the agent's own call: the MCP door's `present_question`. |
| [`QuoteState`](#quotestate) | type | How a quote was found in its source: whole, reformatted, stitched from parts in order or out of order, or not found; `unquoted` is for a value given with no quote. |
| [`ReclaimWay`](#reclaimway) | type | Free a held step so it can run again: a person's act, never an agent's. |
| [`RefusedCheck`](#refusedcheck) | type | The checks other than capability that refuse a step before its claim (`checkPreClaim`). |
| [`RegisterWay`](#registerway) | type | Register the run's workflow again. |
| [`RespondWay`](#respondway) | type | Answer the run's open question. |
| [`RunPhase`](#runphase) | type | Derived phase of a workflow run. |
| [`RunStepWay`](#runstepway) | type | Run one step: an agent step's answer, or an engine step's input given by the operator. |
| [`SideFileKind`](#sidefilekind) | type | One of `SIDE_FILE_KINDS`. |
| [`Slot`](#slot) | type | A value the caller picks from a closed set, printed by each door's own rule (`RespondWay.choice`). |
| [`StoredFileClass`](#storedfileclass) | type | What is wrong with a damaged stored file: empty, not JSON, not a run, filed under another id, from an earlier Realm, or unreadable (`UnreadableFileFacts.class`). |
| [`StoredFileErrorFacts`](#storedfileerrorfacts) | type | The typed facts of a damaged stored file's error: one file (`scope: 'file'`) or a decision over every run that failed closed (`scope: 'files'`). |
| [`Unavailable`](#unavailable) | type | A way that cannot be taken now, with its code, its facts and the remedies that lead on. |
| [`UnavailableCode`](#unavailablecode) | type | The codes that say why a way cannot be taken now, one per reason (`Unavailable.code`). |
| [`WarningCode`](#warningcode) | type | Every warning code the workflow loader can give (`LoaderWarning.code`). |
| [`WayOn`](#wayon) | type | One act a party can take on a run, told apart by its `verb`. |
| [`WayVerb`](#wayverb) | type | The acts a way names: answer a question, run a step, have the engine carry out what it owes, read the run, end it, register its workflow again, or send a question's form to the person (`Base.verb`). |
| [`WorkflowCopyFault`](#workflowcopyfault) | type | What a registered copy that is a JSON object lacks to be a workflow: a numeric `schema_version`, an `id`, `steps`, or the legacy shape. |
| [`COND_TAGS`](#cond_tags) | const | Who discharges a condition outside Realm: `client`, the MCP client's own approval prompt. |
| [`DEFINITION_ABSENCES`](#definition_absences) | const | How a `definition_absent` code arose: one per arm of `getWorkflowForRun`. |
| [`LEASE_PROBE_REASONS`](#lease_probe_reasons) | const | Why a probe could not say whether a lease is held: a closed list. |
| [`QUOTE_STATES`](#quote_states) | const | How a quote was found in its source, rung by rung: `exact`, `reformatted`, `stitched`, `stitched_out_of_order` or `not_found`, and the handler's `unquoted`. |
| [`SIDE_FILE_KINDS`](#side_file_kinds) | const | The kinds of side file a run keeps beside its file in its runs folder: failed attempts, a trace buffer, and sealed traces. |
| [`STORED_FILE_CLASSES`](#stored_file_classes) | const | The kinds of fault a damaged stored JSON file can have (`UnreadableFileFacts.class`). |
| [`UNAVAILABLE_CODES`](#unavailable_codes) | const | The codes that say why a way is unavailable, each with how it is judged and the verbs it applies to. |
| [`WAY_VERBS`](#way_verbs) | const | Every verb a way can name, as a closed list (`WayVerb`). |

## Functions

### compareStrings

function · public

Compares two strings using a specified match mode.

`@param` a The string to test.

`@param` b The reference string (pattern for regex/prefix, exact target for exact).

`@param` mode "exact" | "prefix" | "regex"

`@returns` true if a matches b under the given mode.

```ts
function compareStrings(a: string, b: string, mode: 'exact' | 'prefix' | 'regex'): boolean;
```

### countResults

function · public

Counts accepted and rejected candidates and adds a candidates_found total.

candidates_found distinguishes between:
  - wiring failure (candidates_found === 0): no items were located to check
  - validation failure (candidates_found > 0, accepted_count === 0): all failed matching
  - clean pass (accepted_count === candidates_found): all passed

`@param` accepted The accepted candidates from partitionBySubstring.

`@param` rejected The rejected candidates from partitionBySubstring.

`@returns` The counts, as `{ accepted_count, rejected_count, candidates_found }`.

```ts
function countResults(accepted: Record<string, unknown>[], rejected: Record<string, unknown>[]): {
    accepted_count: number;
    rejected_count: number;
    candidates_found: number;
};
```

### createDefaultRegistry

function · public · also exported from `@sensigo/realm-mcp`

Returns an ExtensionRegistry pre-populated with Realm's config-less built-ins: the adapter
`FileSystemAdapter` under `'filesystem'` and the handler `CheckQuotesHandler` under
`'check_quotes'`. Nothing here reads the environment.

Configured adapters (slack, github, …) come from the deployment manifest — declare
them under `adapters:` in realm.yaml and the CLI loader constructs them with their
secret-resolved config. Library consumers composing registries by hand can still
`registry.register(...)` their own instances on top of this.

```ts
function createDefaultRegistry(): ExtensionRegistry;
```

### declareReleaseLine

function · public

Declares that a host's store class (or plain-object store) belongs to this copy of realm. Call it
once, from the `@sensigo/realm` your store imports its errors from.

A class: the line goes on its prototype. A plain object: a non-enumerable own property. A target
that already carries this generation: nothing to do. Another generation: refused.

```ts
function declareReleaseLine(target: object | (abstract new (...args: never[]) => object)): void;
```

### locateQuote

function · public

Locates `quote` in `source` (the ladder above). `minPartChars` (default 20, at least 4) is the
floor every stitched part must reach, in canonical characters. An empty source, an empty quote, or
a quote with no letter or digit is `not_found` with no parts.

```ts
function locateQuote(quote: string, source: string, options?: {
    minPartChars?: number;
}): QuoteCheck;
```

### partitionBySubstring

function · public

Partitions a list of candidate objects into accepted and rejected groups.
A candidate is accepted when the value of candidate[quoteField] appears
as a literal substring of sourceText. Matching is strict — no normalization.

`@param` candidates Array of objects, each expected to have quoteField.

`@param` quoteField The property name holding the quote string to test.

`@param` sourceText The document text to search within.

`@returns` The two groups, as
`{ accepted: Record<string, unknown>[], rejected: Record<string, unknown>[] }`.

```ts
function partitionBySubstring(candidates: Record<string, unknown>[], quoteField: string, sourceText: string): {
    accepted: Record<string, unknown>[];
    rejected: Record<string, unknown>[];
};
```

### resolveResource

function · public

Reads a named field from a prior step's output stored in context.resources.

`@param` resources The context.resources object from StepContext. May be undefined.

`@param` stepId The step whose output to read (e.g. "fetch_document").

`@param` fieldName The field within that step's output (e.g. "text").

`@returns` The field value, or undefined if the step or field is absent.

```ts
function resolveResource(resources: Record<string, unknown> | undefined, stepId: string, fieldName: string): unknown;
```

### walkField

function · public

Recursively walks any value and collects all objects that contain a
property named fieldName.

`@param` data The value to walk. Can be any JSON-compatible value.

`@param` fieldName The property name to search for.

`@returns` An array of every object (not array) that has fieldName as
a direct own property.

```ts
function walkField(data: unknown, fieldName: string): Record<string, unknown>[];
```

## Classes

### WorkflowError

class · public (beta: refusal): those members may change in a minor release until they settle

The error Realm throws and records, carrying a code, a category and what the agent does next. A
handler throws one with `retryable: true` to have its step tried again when the step has a
`retry` block.

```ts
class WorkflowError extends Error {
    readonly code: ErrorCode;
    readonly category: ErrorCategory;
    readonly agentAction: AgentAction;
    readonly retryable: boolean;
    readonly details: Record<string, unknown>;
    readonly facts?: ErrorFacts;
    readonly about?: string;
    readonly remedy?: readonly WayOn[];
    readonly refusal?: Unavailable;
    readonly stepId?: string;
    readonly attempt: number;
    readonly retry_after?: number;
    warnings?: readonly LoaderWarning[];
    errors?: readonly string[];
    constructor(message: string, options: WorkflowErrorOptions);
}
```

## Interfaces

### AnswererMismatchFacts

interface · public

The facts of an answer refused because its sender may not answer the question: the names that
may, and the account the channel reported. The names are as written: the question's `owner` and
`answerers`, or the project's list.

```ts
interface AnswererMismatchFacts {
    allowed: readonly string[];
    sender: string;
}
```

### Base

interface · public

What every way carries: its verb and the conditions it is offered with; each way type adds its
own fields to it.

```ts
interface Base<V extends WayVerb> {
    readonly verb: V;
    readonly conditions: readonly Cond[];
}
```

### DueExpiry

interface · public

An open question whose time is up and whose `on_expiry` the engine can carry out (`expiry_due`).

```ts
interface DueExpiry {
    gate_id: string;
    step: string;
    on_expiry: 'settle_default' | 'abort';
}
```

### ErrorFactsByCode

interface · public

The error codes whose facts are typed: one facts type per code, entering with the unit that types
it.
Every other code keeps its untyped `details` until its owning
unit types it (#759 typed the two validation codes; `VALIDATION_EXHAUSTED` and
`VALIDATION_TRACE_SCHEMA` stay untyped until their owners type them).

```ts
interface ErrorFactsByCode {
    RESOURCE_FORMAT_INVALID: StoredFileErrorFacts;
    ENGINE_STORE_FAILED: StoredFileErrorFacts;
    STATE_LEGACY_FORMAT: Extract<StoredFileErrorFacts, {
        scope: 'file';
    }>;
    VALIDATION_INPUT_SCHEMA: ValidationErrorFacts;
    VALIDATION_OUTPUT_SCHEMA: ValidationErrorFacts;
    STATE_NEWER_FORMAT: NewerDefinitionFacts;
    STATE_ANSWERER_MISMATCH: AnswererMismatchFacts;
}
```

### ExtensionIdentityEntry

interface · public

One point-in-time identity of the extension code executing a run. Appended to
`RunRecord.extension_identity` on change (history, newest last). The shape is
load-bearing evidence — never collapsible to a boolean.

```ts
interface ExtensionIdentityEntry {
    captured_at: string;
    pid?: number;
    modules: ExtensionIdentityModule[];
    tree: ExtensionIdentityTree;
    signals?: ExtensionIdentitySignals;
    coverage: 'dir_tree_v1';
    manifest?: {
        path: string;
        content_hash: string;
        secrets_block_hash?: string;
    };
    secret_names?: string[];
    override_active?: true;
    error?: string;
    origin?: 'start';
}
```

### ExtensionIdentityModule

interface · public

One loaded extension module's identity.

```ts
interface ExtensionIdentityModule {
    declared: string;
    resolved: string;
    entry_hash: string;
    format: 'esm' | 'cjs' | 'ts-jiti';
}
```

### ExtensionIdentitySignals

interface · public

Labeled advisory signals — each independently fail-soft; never part of the comparison.

```ts
interface ExtensionIdentitySignals {
    package_version?: string;
    git_head?: string;
}
```

### ExtensionIdentityTree

interface · public

Versioned deterministic directory-tree fingerprint over the module roots.

```ts
interface ExtensionIdentityTree {
    roots: string[];
    rules: string;
    file_count: number;
    total_bytes: number;
    tree_hash: string;
    truncated: boolean;
}
```

### LoaderWarning

interface · public

A single structured diagnostic. `message` is the full human-readable text, minted once at the
source (`findUnknownKeys` below, for the unknown-key family) — `renderLoaderWarning` never
reconstructs it from the structured fields; it only ECHOES `message` verbatim, prefixed with
`⚠ `. `scope` is always present. `id`/`step`/`key`/`did_you_mean` are populated by the
unknown-key family and by the codes that name a specific key — `SCHEMA_STRICT_ADVISORY` carries
the schema key plus a position (issue #586), and `AUTHOR_TEXT_NAMES_ANSWER_TOOL` the field whose
text names the tool (`instructions` or `protocol`, `yaml-loader.ts`). They exist for consumers that want the PARTS (a machine reader, a
different renderer), not for `renderLoaderWarning` to recompose from — that would risk a second,
drifting copy of the same prose. Codes that name nothing narrower than their scope carry just
`code`/`severity`/`message`.

```ts
interface LoaderWarning {
    code: WarningCode;
    severity: 'warn' | 'error';
    message: string;
    scope: 'workflow' | 'step';
    id?: string;
    step?: string;
    key?: string;
    did_you_mean?: string;
    line?: number;
    column?: number;
    endLine?: number;
    endColumn?: number;
    release_line?: {
        project: {
            version: string;
            path: string;
            installed_by: string;
        };
        engine: {
            version: string;
            path: string;
        };
    };
}
```

### NewerDefinitionFacts

interface · public

The facts of a registered workflow copy written by a later Realm: the copy's path, the definition
format it states, and the latest this version reads.
Its own `scope`: the copy is not damaged, so
the damaged-file readers (`unreadableFactsOf`, keyed on `scope: 'file'`) must never take it, and no
damaged-file class (`legacy` is an OLDER format) is true of it.

```ts
interface NewerDefinitionFacts {
    scope: 'newer_definition';
    path?: string;
    schema_version: number;
    reads_up_to: number;
}
```

### PreconditionFacts

interface · public

A failed precondition: its expression and the value read, escaped and bounded
(`PreClaimRefused.precondition`).

```ts
interface PreconditionFacts {
    expression: string;
    value: string;
}
```

### Processor

interface · public

A program's step that changes content, registered under its `id` and run in order by
`runPipeline`.

```ts
interface Processor {
    readonly id: string;
    process(content: ProcessorInput, config: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<ProcessorOutput>;
}
```

### ProcessorInput

interface · public

The text and metadata a processor is given (`Processor.process`).

```ts
interface ProcessorInput {
    text: string;
    metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### ProcessorOutput

interface · public

The text and metadata a processor returns; the next processor in the pipeline is given it.

```ts
interface ProcessorOutput {
    text: string;
    metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### QuoteCheck

interface · public

What `locateQuote` returns for a quote: how it was found, where each part is, how often it
occurs, and the nearest piece when it was not found.

```ts
interface QuoteCheck {
    readonly state: QuoteState;
    readonly parts: readonly QuoteSpan[];
    readonly occurrences: number;
    readonly nearest?: QuoteSpan;
    readonly cut_short?: true;
    readonly cut_short_at?: readonly number[];
}
```

### QuoteSpan

interface · public

A span of the original source: `source.slice(start, end)`.

```ts
interface QuoteSpan {
    readonly start: number;
    readonly end: number;
}
```

### RateLimitConfig

interface · public

How fast Realm calls a service: requests per second, the burst it allows, and how long it waits
after a 429 (`ServiceDefinition.rate_limit`).

```ts
interface RateLimitConfig {
    requests_per_second?: number;
    burst?: number;
    fallback_retry_seconds?: number;
    min_retry_seconds?: number;
    max_retry_seconds?: number;
}
```

### RateLimiter

interface · public

Controls the rate at which requests are sent to an external service.

The engine calls `acquire()` before each adapter invocation when a service
has a `rate_limit` configuration. It calls `pause()` when the service responds
with HTTP 429 to hold off concurrent retries for the indicated window.

```ts
interface RateLimiter {
    acquire(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
    pause(seconds: number): void;
}
```

### RunRecordFieldProblem

interface · public

One field a value lacks, or holds with the wrong type. Names only: never the value.

```ts
interface RunRecordFieldProblem {
    field: string;
    problem: 'missing' | 'wrong_type';
}
```

### ServiceAdapter

interface · public

Service adapter — handles communication with a specific external API.

Implementors that perform multi-step operations (paginated fetch, multi-part upload,
sequential writes) must check `signal?.aborted` between steps and throw if true.
Passing the signal to native `fetch()` handles single-request cancellation automatically.

Method semantics:
- `fetch`  — read or query; must be safe and idempotent.
- `create` — write a new resource; may be non-idempotent.
- `update` — mutate an existing resource; typically idempotent when addressed by ID.
- `delete` — remove an existing resource. Optional: only implement when the adapter
             supports deletion. The engine throws `ADAPTER_OP_UNSUPPORTED` if a workflow
             step requests `service_method: delete` but the adapter omits this method.

```ts
interface ServiceAdapter {
    readonly id: string;
    readonly defaultRetryAfterSeconds?: number;
    readonly config_schema?: Record<string, unknown>;
    fetch(operation: string, params: Record<string, unknown>, config: Record<string, unknown>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ServiceResponse>;
    create(operation: string, params: Record<string, unknown>, config: Record<string, unknown>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ServiceResponse>;
    update(operation: string, params: Record<string, unknown>, config: Record<string, unknown>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ServiceResponse>;
    delete?(operation: string, params: Record<string, unknown>, config: Record<string, unknown>, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ServiceResponse>;
}
```

### ServiceResponse

interface · public

What a service adapter's call returns: the HTTP status and the data (`ServiceAdapter`'s methods).

```ts
interface ServiceResponse {
    status: number;
    data: unknown;
}
```

### StableBoundary

interface · public

Where a rendered text stops repeating between runs, in UTF-16 code units.

```ts
interface StableBoundary {
    chars: number;
    unit: 'utf16';
}
```

### StepBrief

interface · public

What a `run_step` way says about its step: its kind, its description, the prompt the agent reads,
the input schema an agent's answer must fit, and its handler. The prompt is template-resolved;
the handler is a fact kept as data until #516 decides its meaning.

```ts
interface StepBrief {
    execution: 'agent' | 'auto';
    description: string;
    prompt?: string;
    input_schema?: Record<string, unknown>;
    handler?: string;
    stable_prefix?: StableBoundary;
}
```

### StepContext

interface · public

What a handler is told about the run: its id and params, the step's `config`, and earlier steps'
outputs in `resources`, keyed by step id (`StepHandler.execute`'s second argument).

```ts
interface StepContext {
    run_id: string;
    run_params: Record<string, unknown>;
    config: Record<string, unknown>;
    resources?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### StepHandler

interface · public

A program's code for an `auto` step named by `handler:`: registered under its `id`, and called
with the step's input and the run's context.

```ts
interface StepHandler {
    readonly id: string;
    readonly uses_resources?: readonly string[];
    execute(inputs: StepHandlerInputs, context: StepContext, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<StepHandlerResult>;
}
```

### StepHandlerInputs

interface · public

What a handler is given as input: the step's params, after its `input_map` when it has one
(`StepHandler.execute`'s first argument).

```ts
interface StepHandlerInputs {
    params: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

### StepHandlerResult

interface · public

What a handler returns: the step's output, and optionally a state update, a clean abort or a
warning (`StepHandler.execute`'s result).

```ts
interface StepHandlerResult {
    data?: Record<string, unknown>;
    state_update?: Record<string, unknown>;
    abort?: {
        message: string;
    };
    warn?: {
        message: string;
    };
}
```

### UnreadableRunFilesFacts

interface · public

What `unreadableRunFilesError` carries: the command that did not run, the runs folder, and
every run file it could not read.

```ts
interface UnreadableRunFilesFacts {
    command: string;
    folder: string;
    files: UnreadableFileFacts[];
}
```

### ValidationErrorFacts

interface · public

The typed facts of a refused answer: the validator's rows, their total before the cap, and, for
an agent step's counted rejection, the countdown. `errors` are in Ajv's own order, capped at
`VALIDATION_PROBLEMS_SHOWN`, never re-sorted or de-duplicated; `error_count` is counted once at
the validator and carried, never recounted by a renderer; `rejections` and `threshold` are the
countdown.

```ts
interface ValidationErrorFacts {
    errors: readonly ErrorObject[];
    error_count: number;
    rejections?: number;
    threshold?: number;
}
uses ErrorObject (ajv 8)
```

### WorkflowErrorOptions

interface · public (beta: refusal): those members may change in a minor release until they settle

What a `WorkflowError` is built with: its code and category, what the agent does next, whether it
may be tried again, and the optional facts, step and ways on.

```ts
interface WorkflowErrorOptions {
    code: ErrorCode;
    category: ErrorCategory;
    agentAction: AgentAction;
    retryable: boolean;
    details?: Record<string, unknown>;
    facts?: ErrorFacts;
    about?: string;
    remedy?: readonly WayOn[];
    refusal?: Unavailable;
    stepId?: string;
    attempt?: number;
    retry_after?: number;
    warnings?: readonly LoaderWarning[];
    errors?: readonly string[];
}
```

## Types

### AbandonWay

type · public

End the run.

```ts
type AbandonWay = Base<'abandon'> & {
    run_id: string;
};
```

### AdvanceWay

type · public

Have the engine carry out what it owes: a due expiry first, then steps.

```ts
type AdvanceWay = Base<'advance'> & {
    run_id: string;
    owed: readonly ({
        step: string;
    } | {
        expiry: DueExpiry;
    })[];
};
```

### AgentAction

type · public

What an agent does next, decided by the engine (`WorkflowError.agentAction`).
`wait_for_service`: an outside service is unavailable —
wait, then try again (issue #729 PR-0, D4 P-2: renamed from `wait_for_human`, every vocabulary read
uses "human" for a person). `await`: the run waits on someone else — a person's answer or another
program's step (D3 A-2); its replies carry `poll_after_ms` and, when the record states one, `until`.

```ts
type AgentAction = 'report_to_user' | 'provide_input' | 'resolve_precondition' | 'stop' | 'wait_for_service' | 'wait_and_proceed' | 'await';
```

### Cond

type · public

A condition a way is offered with: a way offered with a condition is admitted only when the
condition is met (`Base.conditions`).
PR-0's one member: `enactor_has` — the step needs a handler or
an adapter, and whether this program has it is judged from its `basis`: `marker` (the run's own
`capability_blocks` record: the program that last attempted the step lacked it), `unjudged` (an
observer passed no registry — C33: a read surface never executes project code), `load_failed` (this
program's project code failed to load).

W added `client_prompt`; PR-1 adds `confirm_after_preview`, `erases_operator_ending`,
`override_claim_unknown_age` — each with its producer, never reserved here. The gate-answers default
(2026-11-14) removed `client_prompt`'s one producer, the MCP door's fallback row; the member and its
tag stay, as exported names, and nothing composes it now.

```ts
type Cond = {
    code: 'enactor_has';
    kind: 'handler' | 'adapter';
    name: string;
    basis: 'marker' | 'unjudged' | 'load_failed';
} | {
    code: 'client_prompt';
    tag: CondTag;
} | {
    code: 'claim_deadline_ahead';
    deadline: string;
} | {
    code: 'override_claim_unknown_age';
    state: 'unknown_age' | 'unreadable' | 'no_claim_record';
} | {
    code: 'rerun_not_idempotent';
    basis: 'not_declared' | 'definition_absent';
};
```

### CondTag

type · public

Who discharges a condition outside Realm; `client` is the MCP client's own approval prompt
(`Cond`'s `client_prompt` member).

```ts
type CondTag = (typeof COND_TAGS)[number];
```

### DefinitionAbsence

type · public

Why a run's workflow definition could not be had: never registered, an agent's copy gone,
unreadable, not a valid workflow, an older or a later format, or not read.

```ts
type DefinitionAbsence = (typeof DEFINITION_ABSENCES)[number];
```

### ErrorCategory

type · public

The broad kind of failure a `WorkflowError` reports: network, an outside service, the run's
state, invalid input, the engine itself, or a resource (`WorkflowError.category`).

```ts
type ErrorCategory = 'NETWORK' | 'SERVICE' | 'STATE' | 'VALIDATION' | 'ENGINE' | 'RESOURCE';
```

### ErrorFacts

type · public

Any typed error facts.

```ts
type ErrorFacts = ErrorFactsByCode[keyof ErrorFactsByCode];
```

### FactsOf

type · public

The typed facts an `Unavailable` entry carries for its code (`Unavailable.facts`).

```ts
type FactsOf<C extends UnavailableCode> = FactsByCode[C];
```

### InspectWay

type · public

Read the run's record.

```ts
type InspectWay = Base<'inspect'> & {
    run_id: string;
};
```

### LeaseFact

type · public

What a probe found. `unknown` always carries its reason; the other three never do.

```ts
type LeaseFact = {
    readonly state: 'held' | 'not_held' | 'absent';
    readonly basis: 'kernel_lock';
} | {
    readonly state: 'unknown';
    readonly basis: 'kernel_lock';
    readonly reason: LeaseProbeReason;
};
```

### LeaseProbeReason

type · public

Why a probe could not say whether a claim lease is held (`LeaseFact`'s `unknown` state).

```ts

```

### LoadErrorCode

type · public

The code a failed load of a program's project code carries: the error's catalogue code, or
`uncoded`. The loader throws plain errors too, and no catalogue code is minted for them (a reader
is never sent to the catalogue for a code that is not there).

```ts
type LoadErrorCode = ErrorCode | 'uncoded';
```

### NoRemedy

type · public

Why an `Unavailable` entry offers no way on, with the cause's own facts
(`Unavailable.no_remedy`).

```ts
type NoRemedy = {
    cause: 'operator_command_untyped';
    command: 'resume' | 'drain' | 'purge' | 'start';
} | {
    cause: 'requires_other_program';
    requirement: {
        kind: 'handler' | 'adapter';
        name: string;
    };
} | {
    cause: 'another_program_holds_it';
} | {
    cause: 'already_settled';
} | {
    cause: 'engine_runs_it_when_owed';
};
```

### PresentWay

type · public

Show the open question again, as a form in the agent's own call: the MCP door's
`present_question`.
The agent cannot answer through it: the person's accept records the
answer. No `step`: a renderer reads the step from the reply it already holds.

```ts
type PresentWay = Base<'present'> & {
    run_id: string;
    gate_id: string;
};
```

### QuoteState

type · public

How a quote was found in its source: whole, reformatted, stitched from parts in order or out of
order, or not found; `unquoted` is for a value given with no quote.

```ts
type QuoteState = (typeof QUOTE_STATES)[number];
```

### ReclaimWay

type · public

Free a held step so it can run again: a person's act, never an agent's. Its conditions say what
holds, each discharged by `force`; `claimed_at` is the claim's stamp, present exactly when the claim
carries one, so the act applies only to the claim it was shown (#922).

```ts
type ReclaimWay = Base<'reclaim'> & {
    run_id: string;
    step: string;
    claimed_at?: string;
};
```

### RefusedCheck

type · public

The checks other than capability that refuse a step before its claim (`checkPreClaim`).

```ts
type RefusedCheck = 'trust' | 'precondition' | 'input_schema';
```

### RegisterWay

type · public

Register the run's workflow again. No judge admits it; on MCP it is the operator's, done outside
the conversation (the door renders no instruction).
`path` only
when the registry knows the file (T-21: the unreadable, invalid, legacy and newer copies carry
it): the registered COPY that cannot be used — never a file to register (correction 2, 3.2: each
door words it as a copy to repair).

`copy` (#616 PR-2c c10a-4c) says the registered copy EXISTS but cannot be used, whether or not it
has a file: a copy in a database has none, so `path` alone cannot tell it from a copy that is not
there. The doors read it; the library's own words (`LIBRARY_WORDS`) do not, because the library's
repair is the same act either way.

```ts
type RegisterWay = Base<'register'> & {
    workflow_id: string;
    run_id?: string;
    path?: string;
    copy?: 'unusable';
};
```

type · public

Answer the run's open question.

```ts
    expires_at?: string;
    on_expiry?: 'settle_default' | 'abort';

    presented: 'with_gate' | 'alone';
    has_message?: true;
    owner?: string;
    proof?: {
        claim_token: string;
    };
};
```

type · public

Derived phase of a workflow run. Always computed from the four step sets and run state;
never set directly by callers outside the engine.

```ts
type RunPhase = 'running' | 'gate_waiting' | 'completed' | 'failed' | 'abandoned' | 'aborted';
```

### RunStepWay

type · public

Run one step: an agent step's answer, or an engine step's input given by the operator.

```ts
type RunStepWay = Base<'run_step'> & {
    run_id: string;
    step: string;
    brief: StepBrief;
};
```

### SideFileKind

type · public

One of `SIDE_FILE_KINDS`.

```ts
type SideFileKind = (typeof SIDE_FILE_KINDS)[number];
```

### Slot

type · public

A value the caller picks from a closed set, printed by each door's own rule
(`RespondWay.choice`).

```ts

    readonly one_of: readonly T[];
```

### StoredFileClass

type · public

What is wrong with a damaged stored file: empty, not JSON, not a run, filed under another id,

```ts

```

type · public

The typed facts of a damaged stored file's error: one file (`scope: 'file'`) or a decision over

The aggregate shares both of

type · public

### COND_TAGS

const · public

Who discharges a condition outside Realm: `client`, the MCP client's own approval prompt.
Beside `Cond`, never on `CODE_TAGS`, which tags UNAVAILABLE codes.
OFFER_EQUALS_ADMISSION compares offer and admission over conditions Realm judges, so it leaves a
`client`-tagged condition out of the compared set.

```ts
const COND_TAGS: readonly [
    "client"
];
```

### DEFINITION_ABSENCES

const · public

How a `definition_absent` code arose: one per arm of `getWorkflowForRun`.

```ts
const DEFINITION_ABSENCES: readonly [
    "agent_copy_gone",
    "not_registered",
    "unreadable",
    "format_invalid",
    "legacy",
    "not_read",
    "newer"
];
```

### LEASE_PROBE_REASONS

const · public

Why a probe could not say whether a lease is held: a closed list. `not_checked` is for a caller that
did not probe at all (from CW-1b); the store's probe answers the other four.

```ts
const LEASE_PROBE_REASONS: readonly [
    "not_checked",
    "cannot_open",
    "not_a_lease",
    "permission",
    "io_error"
];
```

### QUOTE_STATES

const · public

How a quote was found in its source, rung by rung: `exact`, `reformatted`, `stitched`,
`stitched_out_of_order` or `not_found`, and the handler's `unquoted`.

locateQuote — whether, and how, a quote appears in a source text (issue #760; design D2, D3, D6;
correction 1: the locating rule A1–A9, the stitching rule S, the leftovers L1–L4).

The ONE implementation of the quote ladder and of the canonical form; the `check_quotes` handler
calls it and composes nothing of its own. It never judges whether a value is correct — only
whether, and how, its quote is in the source.

The ladder, first hit wins:
- `exact`: the quote is a literal substring of the source.
- `reformatted`: the quote's canonical form is a substring of the source's canonical form.
- `stitched`: the quote breaks — at `…` / `...`, a sentence end, `;`, a `:` not between two digits,
  a double quotation mark or a line break — and every piece between its breaks is found whole, at
  word and number edges, in the order quoted. Pieces that sit next to each other in the source
  count as one part, and every part is at least `minPartChars` canonical characters. Text is
  skipped only between parts, never inside a piece (the owner's yes, 2026-10-18).
- `stitched_out_of_order`: the same, with the parts in another order.
- `not_found`: otherwise; `nearest` is the longest piece of the quote found in the source, when it
  covers at least one whole word.
(`unquoted` is the handler's, for a candidate with no quote and no value; this never returns it.)

A quote that ends a sentence where the source's sentence goes on is marked `cut_short` (L2). Every
offset is a UTF-16 code-unit offset into the ORIGINAL source.

```ts
const QUOTE_STATES: readonly [
    "exact",
    "reformatted",
    "stitched",
    "stitched_out_of_order",
    "not_found",
    "unquoted"
];
```

### SIDE_FILE_KINDS

const · public

The kinds of side file a run keeps beside its file in its runs folder: failed attempts, a trace
buffer, and sealed traces.

```ts
const SIDE_FILE_KINDS: readonly [
    "attempts",
    "trace_buffer",
    "sealed_trace"
];
```

### STORED_FILE_CLASSES

const · public

The kinds of fault a damaged stored JSON file can have (`UnreadableFileFacts.class`). They are the
registrar's listing's words, plus the run-only classes:
 - `empty`: zero bytes, or whitespace only;
 - `parse`: not JSON, or JSON that is not an object (`shape` says what it is);
 - `not_a_run`: an object that is not a run record (`fields` names what is missing or mistyped);
 - `mismatched`: a run record whose `id` is not the file's name (`held_id`, `held_file`);
 - `legacy`: written by an earlier Realm (`state` without `completed_steps`);
 - `unreadable`: the file (or the runs folder) cannot be read (`errno`).

```ts
const STORED_FILE_CLASSES: readonly [
    "empty",
    "parse",
    "not_a_run",
    "mismatched",
    "legacy",
    "unreadable"
];
```

### WAY_VERBS

const · public

Every verb a way can name, as a closed list (`WayVerb`).

PR-0's verbs (option B) and #627 W's `present` (Amendment 2): PR-1 adds resume/drain/purge, PR-2
reclaim/validate/export, PR-7 start.

```ts
const WAY_VERBS: readonly [
    "respond",
    "run_step",
    "advance",
    "inspect",
    "abandon",
    "register",
    "present",
    "reclaim"
];
```

## Also used by this job

Names this job reaches whose entry is on another page.

- [`ErrorCode`](define-and-load-a-workflow.md#errorcode): Every code a `WorkflowError` can carry, grouped by its category; a reply's error and the error catalogue name it (`WorkflowError.code`).
- [`ExtensionRegistry`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#extensionregistry): The handlers, service adapters and processors a program registers by name; the engine looks a step's handler or adapter up in it.
- [`UnreadableFileFacts`](run-and-drive-a-run.md#unreadablefilefacts): The facts of one damaged stored file: names, classes and type words, never its content.
